# Case mapping

Simple and full upper, lower and title case mappings, and case folding.

<h2 id="to-upper-simple"><code>ToUpperSimple</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ToUpperSimple(scalar: char32) -> char32
```

The simple uppercase of `scalar`: one value to one, itself when it has no mapping.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Unicode/Src/Case.rux#L18)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type     | Description             |
| -------- | -------- | ----------------------- |
| `scalar` | `char32` | the scalar value to map |

**Returns**: its single-scalar uppercase, or `scalar` itself when there is none

<h2 id="to-upper-full"><code>ToUpperFull</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ToUpperFull(scalar: char32, into: var char32[..], written: *var uint) -> bool
```

Writes the full uppercase of `scalar` into `into` and reports how many values it took.
Up to three values, so a buffer of three always suffices; reports `false` without writing when the room is
short. Falls back to the simple mapping for the points that need no expansion, which is nearly all of them.
`written` must be non-null and writable.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Unicode/Src/Case.rux#L77)

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type             | Description                                       |
| --------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `scalar`  | `char32`         | the scalar value to map                           |
| `into`    | `var char32[..]` | receives the mapping; three values always suffice |
| `written` | `*var uint`      | receives how many values were written             |

**Returns**: false without writing when `into` is too short

<h2 id="fold"><code>Fold</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Fold(scalar: char32, into: var char32[..], written: *var uint) -> bool
```

Writes the full, locale-independent case folding of `scalar` into `into`.
Folding is for comparison rather than display: fold both strings, and equal foldings mean the same text
whatever its case. It is built from the C and F entries alone, which is what makes the answer the same in every
locale. A point with no entry folds to itself.
`written` must be non-null and writable.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Unicode/Src/Case.rux#L102)

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type             | Description                                       |
| --------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `scalar`  | `char32`         | the scalar value to fold                          |
| `into`    | `var char32[..]` | receives the folding; three values always suffice |
| `written` | `*var uint`      | receives how many values were written             |

**Returns**: false without writing when `into` is too short
